name: Engineering Services Examination
department: Rules notified by the Department of Telecommunications; posts across Railways, CPWD, Defence, Telecom, Water, Power and other ministries
summary: The main national exam for Group A engineering officers of the Government of India, in four branches: Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, and Electronics and Telecommunication. It has three stages: an objective Prelims (500 marks), a descriptive Mains (600 marks) and a 200-mark interview. Unlike CSE, Prelims marks count in the final rank of 1300.

status.note: Held every year. Usual pattern: notification in September, Prelims in January or February, Mains in June, interviews in the following months, and the final result later in the year.

age.summary: At least 21 and under 30 years on 1 January of the exam year. For ESE 2027: born between 2 January 1997 and 1 January 2006.
age.referenceDate: 1 January of the exam year (1 Jan 2027 for ESE 2027)

relaxations.category: Ex-servicemen incl. ECO/SSCO with 5 years service (conditions apply)
PwBD (low vision, deaf/hard of hearing, locomotor, SLD, mental illness)

relaxations.note: Upper limit up to 35 for permanent staff, or temporary staff with 3 years regular service, applying to services of their own department.

eligibility.nationality: Citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or other specified categories with a Government of India eligibility certificate.

education.summary: A degree in engineering, or Sections A and B of the Institution of Engineers (India), or other listed equivalents (IETE graduate membership, Aeronautical Society of India associate membership, and so on). For Indian Naval Armament Service (electronics) and Indian Radio Regulatory Service, an M.Sc. with wireless communication, electronics, radio physics or radio engineering is also accepted.

attempts.limit: No limit on attempts (within age limit)

eligibility.physical: Physical and medical standards as in the ESE Rules. Some services (for example Border Roads) have additional field requirements.
other: You write the exam in one branch (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical or E&T); you can only be allocated services of that branch.
eligibility.examVsPost: You choose one engineering category when applying, and you can be allotted only the services in that category. Some services in the list are Group B (for example Junior Telecom Officer) and pay below Level 10.
disqualifications: Applications cannot be withdrawn after submission.
eligibility.reservation: Central reservation: SC 15%, ST 7.5%, OBC 27%, EWS 10%, plus PwBD. ESE 2027 has about 480 vacancies including 19 for PwBD.

eligibilityRules.notes: Upper limit means under 30 on 1 Jan 2027 (up to 29 completed years). Some electronics posts also accept a relevant M.Sc.

stages.name: Stage I: Preliminary (objective)

papers.name: Paper I: General Studies and Engineering Aptitude (common to all)
papers.negative: One third of the question's marks

papers.name: Paper II: your engineering branch
papers.negative: One third of the question's marks

stages.notes: Minimum qualifying marks are set in both papers. About 6 to 7 times the vacancies are admitted to Mains. Prelims marks are counted in the final merit.

stages.name: Stage II: Main (conventional)
stages.notes: Answered in English only. About twice the vacancies are called for interview.

stages.name: Stage III: Personality Test
stages.notes: Assesses leadership, initiative, intellectual curiosity, tact and other social qualities, mental and physical energy, practical application and integrity.

selection.meritCalculation: Final marks = Prelims (500) + Mains (600) + Personality Test (200) = 1300.
selection.tieBreaking: (1) Higher marks in the three engineering papers (Prelims Paper II and Mains Papers I and II) plus the interview; (2) then the three engineering papers alone; (3) then the older candidate; (4) any remaining tie at the Commission's discretion. Marks are rounded to two decimals.
selection.normalization: None; each branch writes the same papers.
selection.languages: All papers are set in English and conventional papers must be answered in English.
selection.documentVerification: Original documents are produced at the interview.
selection.probation: Service-specific training and probation as per each service's rules.

sections.subject: Paper I: General Studies and Engineering Aptitude
topics: Current issues of national and international importance in social, economic and industrial development
Engineering aptitude: logical reasoning and analytical ability
General principles of design, drawing, importance of safety
Standards and quality practices in production, construction, maintenance and services
Basics of energy and environment: conservation, pollution, climate change, environmental impact assessment
Basics of material science and engineering
ICT tools and their engineering uses: networking, e-governance, technology-based education
Ethics and values in the engineering profession

sections.subject: Branch papers (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical or E&T)
topics: The same branch syllabus is used for the Prelims objective Paper II and the two Mains conventional papers
Standard: roughly an engineering degree examination of an Indian university
Full topic lists for each branch are in Section III of the notification

supplementary: Each of the 10 Paper I topics carries roughly 5% to 15% of that paper's marks, as stated in the notification.
Candidates often prepare ESE alongside GATE, because the branch syllabus overlaps heavily.

workLife.postings: Anywhere in India, including project sites, border areas (Border Roads) and defence establishments.
workLife.nature: Mix of field engineering (construction, maintenance, operations) and office work.
workLife.workload: Project deadlines and operations can mean long hours.
workLife.hazards: Construction and field-site risks; remote postings for some services.

difficulty.rationale: Full engineering-degree syllabus, tested both objectively and in long answers. Competition is lower than CSE in candidates per vacancy (2023: 33,864 appeared for about 486 vacancies, about 70 per vacancy). Prelims, Mains and interview all count.

ratings.rationale: Annual exam leading to Group A engineering services. Postings depend on the service and are often outside big cities.

factors.note: Vacancies have ranged from about 250 to 500 in recent years.

factors.note: UPSC annual reports note results for some vacancies being declared later.

sections.title: What ESE is for
paragraphs: ESE (often called IES) is UPSC's exam for engineer officers in central services: Railways, CPWD, Telecom, Defence engineering, the Central Water and Power services, and others. You pick one branch, Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, or Electronics and Telecommunication, and compete only within it.

sections.title: Stage I: Prelims
paragraphs: Paper I (200 marks, 2 hours) is common to all branches: general studies and engineering aptitude, covering ten fixed topics. Paper II (300 marks, 3 hours) is your branch. UPSC sets minimum marks in both papers and admits about 6 to 7 times the vacancies to Mains.
Unlike the Civil Services Exam, ESE Prelims marks are added to your final total, so every mark matters.

sections.title: Stage II: Mains
paragraphs: Two long-answer papers in your branch, in English. The syllabus is the same branch syllabus as Prelims Paper II, but answers must show derivations, design reasoning and numerical working.

sections.title: Stage III: Personality Test
paragraphs: The board looks for leadership, initiative and intellectual curiosity, tact and other social qualities, mental and physical energy, practical application, and integrity. Expect questions on your engineering background and projects.

sections.title: Common confusions
bullets: ESE has no attempt limit; only the age limit (under 30 on 1 January, with relaxations) applies.
Age is counted on 1 January of the exam year, not 1 August as in CSE.
Not every ESE service is Group A: Junior Telecom Officer is Group B.
IRMS engineering posts (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, S&T, Stores) are filled through ESE; IRMS Traffic, Personnel and Accounts come through CSE.
